objectives.title: Recognize verbs used with instrumental complements

steps.bookDirection: Open Lesson 16 in the copy you own. The app records do not replace that lesson.

steps.title: One noun, different cases
steps.body: The instrumental case can mark the means used to do something. These checks first teach its forms. сто́л is the dictionary form, meaning table; столо́м is instrumental singular. The word still names a table: the ending marks its grammatical role, not a new vocabulary meaning.

steps.title: A bounded noun ending
steps.body: The instrumental singular -ом fits the hard stem of the relevant noun class. Soft stems use their own instrumental ending, so -ом is not universal. Here, keep the stem of сто́л and add -ом to obtain столо́м. Learn the stress with the whole form.

steps.title: Compare the other cases
steps.body: столу́ is dative singular and столе́ is prepositional singular. Both belong to the same noun, but neither has the instrumental singular ending. For an instrumental singular request, select столо́м rather than selecting a form merely because its English gloss is table.

steps.title: Work the house form
steps.body: до́м means house in its dictionary form. до́мом is instrumental singular: keep the stem and add -ом. Given до́м and an instrumental singular request, choose до́мом. This is the same ending pattern as the table form.

steps.title: Check case before choosing
steps.body: до́му is dative singular; до́ме is prepositional singular. They do not answer an instrumental singular request. Compare the entire ending with до́мом, and notice that this noun keeps its stem stress.

steps.title: Meaning and form together
steps.body: поездом is instrumental singular of the noun meaning train; карандашом is instrumental singular of the noun meaning pencil. The pencil check asks for that meaning as well as the case. Its other options refer to train and husband. A correct case alone does not identify the requested noun.

steps.title: A different singular pattern
steps.body: книгой is the instrumental singular form for book. This noun has a different ending from the -ом shown for table and house. Do not attach the same ending to every noun. These examples introduce selected singular patterns, not the full instrumental paradigm.

steps.body: Identify the requested case and number, then compare the displayed forms. A missed check returns to the full explanation and examples.

steps.title: Instrumental plural of book
steps.body: Instrumental plural refers to more than one. кни́га is the dictionary singular form for book; кни́гами is instrumental plural. Keep the stem and use -ами in this pattern. Given an instrumental plural request, choose кни́гами.

steps.title: Plural noun endings
steps.body: Instrumental plural nouns commonly use -ами or -ями, with exceptions. The book, house and table forms shown here use -ами. This is a noun ending; adjectives have their own agreement endings. These checks ask you to recognize the displayed pattern, not derive every noun form.

steps.title: Compare plural cases
steps.body: кни́гам is dative plural; кни́гах is prepositional plural. Neither is instrumental plural. Compare their endings with кни́гами: the final vowel is part of the instrumental plural ending here.

steps.title: Work the house plural
steps.body: до́м names a house in the dictionary singular. дома́ми is instrumental plural. For this plural case request choose дома́ми, including the stress shown in the retained form.

steps.title: Case and number both matter
steps.body: дома́м is dative plural. до́мом is instrumental singular. The first has the wrong case; the second has the right case but the wrong number for an instrumental plural request. дома́ми meets both requirements.

steps.title: Work the table plural
steps.body: сто́л is the dictionary singular form for table. стола́ми is instrumental plural. For an instrumental plural request, select стола́ми and learn its stress with the ending.

steps.title: Reject a singular instrumental
steps.body: стола́м is dative plural; столо́м is instrumental singular. Neither meets both parts of an instrumental plural request. стола́ми supplies instrumental case and plural number together.

steps.title: Adjective agreement
steps.body: An adjective agrees with its noun in case and number, and in gender in the singular. хоро́ший is the masculine dictionary form for good. хоро́шим is its masculine or neuter instrumental singular form. Here the check requests masculine instrumental; it does not ask for an English gloss.

steps.title: Adjective endings differ
steps.body: Hard-stem masculine and neuter adjectives take -ым in the instrumental, and the soft or spelling-restricted stems take -им. These are adjective declension endings. хоро́шим uses -им because of the spelling restriction after its stem-final consonant. Do not apply the noun ending -ом to this adjective.

steps.title: Compare dative and plural
steps.body: хоро́шему is dative masculine or neuter singular. хоро́шие is nominative plural. Neither is the masculine instrumental singular form requested here. Work the choice by selecting хоро́шим.

steps.title: Instrumental plural agreement
steps.body: хоро́шими is instrumental plural, with a plural adjective ending. хоро́шая is feminine nominative singular. For a plural instrumental request select хоро́шими; хоро́шим has singular number. Recognizing these forms does not by itself demonstrate using adjective agreement in a sentence.

steps.title: Two meanings of with
steps.body: Я написал хорошим новым карандашом — I wrote with a good new pencil. The pencil is the tool used for writing: this is the means instrumental, without a preposition before the tool phrase. Я хочу встречу с интересной русской женщиной — I want a meeting with an interesting Russian woman. Here with introduces the person involved in the meeting: this is the accompaniment line, using a preposition followed by instrumental forms.

steps.title: Work the role contrast
steps.body: For a means instrumental request, choose the writing sentence because its pencil is the instrument. For an accompaniment line request, choose the meeting sentence because it describes being with a person. English with can express both roles; its presence alone does not decide which Russian construction is used. Read what the phrase contributes to the event.

steps.title: A separate spatial role
steps.body: Я живу́ ме́жду двумя но́выми дома́ми — I live between two new houses. This is the between line: the phrase locates the speaker relative to two houses. The houses are neither a writing tool nor a companion. Work the choice by identifying location rather than treating every instrumental phrase as a means phrase.

steps.title: Guided practice
steps.body: Compare the meanings and roles explained above, then choose from the displayed alternatives. A missed check returns to all explanations and examples.

steps.title: Above and below
steps.body: над — over. под — under. These spatial meanings contrast vertical positions. The over label belongs to the first preposition; the under label belongs to the second. In a location construction, both can govern instrumental forms. The questions here recognize meanings from isolated prepositions; they do not ask you to choose a noun ending.

steps.title: Case depends on the construction
steps.body: The same preposition can govern different cases in different uses. For the preposition meaning under, instrumental describes location, while accusative can describe a destination under something. Movement within a location does not by itself require accusative: distinguish where something is from where it is going. These isolated-word checks contain no movement context and therefore do not assess that case choice.

steps.title: Before and between
steps.body: перед — before. между — between. In the spatial use introduced here, before means in front of; it is not a universal translation for every English time expression with before. Between places something relative to two things. When choosing a displayed English label, compare the specific spatial meaning, including the alternative behind. Learn the meaning first; sentence use still requires the appropriate case.

sessions.title: Recognize verbs used with instrumental complements

steps.title: Becoming and remaining
steps.body: стать means to become. остаться means to remain. Both are infinitives: they name an action or state without marking a past event. Becoming expresses a change; remaining expresses continuation. For the first form choose to become. For the second form choose remain among the displayed choices. The English past-tense word became does not correctly label either infinitive.

steps.title: What a complement describes
steps.body: An instrumental complement can describe the role or state of the subject after a linking verb, rather than an instrument used to carry out an action. The verbs shown in this lesson can occur in that construction. These checks show only the verbs and ask for their meanings. Recognizing a verb meaning is a first step; it does not demonstrate forming a complete sentence with an instrumental complement.

steps.title: Appearance and discovery
steps.body: казаться — appear to be. оказаться — turn out to be. The first concerns how something seems; the second concerns what it proves to be. Work the second choice by selecting turn out to be, rather than the meaning of continuation. A displayed infinitive still does not specify a past event. Keep these meanings distinct from becoming and remaining.
